mcqs.question: A vector of magnitude 10 m makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal. Which of the following statements about its components is correct?

options.C: The sum of the magnitudes of the horizontal and vertical components equals the magnitude of the vector.
options.D: The horizontal component is 10 cos 30° and the vertical component is 10 sin 30°.

mcqs.answer: The horizontal component is 10 cos 30° and the vertical component is 10 sin 30°.
mcqs.explanation: Resolving a vector into perpendicular components uses trigonometric relations: horizontal = magnitude × cos θ, vertical = magnitude × sin θ. For a 10 m vector at 30°, the components are 10 cos 30° ≈ 8.66 m (horizontal) and 10 sin 30° = 5 m (vertical). Options A and B give only one component without the correct relation, and C is a common misconception – the magnitudes of components do not add vectorially to give the original magnitude.

mcqs.question: A displacement vector has magnitude 20 m and is directed 60° north of east. What are its rectangular components (eastward, northward)?
mcqs.explanation: Component along east = 20 cos 60° = 20 × 0.5 = 10 m. Component along north = 20 sin 60° = 20 × √3/2 ≈ 17.32 m. Hence the rectangular components are (10 m east, 17.3 m north). Option B swaps the components, while C and D ignore the angle.

mcqs.question: Two vectors have the following components (in metres): Vector P = 3 i + 4 j, Vector Q = 5 i + 12 j. Which statement is true?

options.A: Both vectors have the same magnitude.
options.B: Vector Q has a larger magnitude than Vector P.
options.C: Vector P has a larger magnitude than Vector Q.
options.D: Their magnitudes cannot be compared without knowing the angle between them.

mcqs.answer: Vector Q has a larger magnitude than Vector P.
mcqs.explanation: Magnitude of a vector = √(x² + y²). For P: √(3² + 4²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5 m. For Q: √(5² + 12²) = √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13 m. Therefore, Q is larger. Option A is false because magnitudes differ; C is opposite; D is unnecessary because magnitudes are obtained directly from components.

mcqs.learning_point: Use component methods in physical problems
mcqs.question: A projectile is launched from ground level with a speed of 50 m/s at an angle of 30° above the horizontal. Ignoring air resistance and taking g = 10 m/s², what is the horizontal range of the projectile?
mcqs.explanation: Resolve the initial velocity: Vₓ = 50 cos 30° = 50 × √3/2 ≈ 43.3 m/s, Vᵧ = 50 sin 30° = 25 m/s. Time of flight = 2Vᵧ/g = 2 × 25/10 = 5 s. Horizontal range = Vₓ × time = 43.3 × 5 ≈ 216.5 m, rounded to 216 m. Options B, C, D are significantly larger and result from incorrect use of trigonometric values or forgetting the factor of 2 in time of flight.
